title: systemd-resolved on linux: compound failure — disk_full + resource_limit
scenario: A production systemd-resolved (dns) on linux will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: the partition holding the data/log dir is at 100% AND a systemd/ulimit resource cap kills the service (OOM/nofile). under capacity pressure both disk and memory limits bite; you must triage which to relieve first. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'disk_full' and 'resource_limit' on systemd-resolved
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `systemd-resolved` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `journalctl -u systemd-resolved -n 120 --no-pager` shows TWO distinct signals ('No space left on device' and 'Killed / too many open files').
Interaction: under capacity pressure both disk and memory limits bite; you must triage which to relieve first.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'disk_full': df to find the full mount; du/ncdu to find the consumer.
Then address 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `systemd-resolved` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 53 if applicable) with BOTH 'disk_full' and 'resource_limit' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Reclamation targets logs/cache only; live data is never deleted, so the action is safe by construction. Limit overrides are drop-in files; revert to restore defaults. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: under capacity pressure both disk and memory limits bite; you must triage which to relieve first

possible_mistakes: delete the service's live database to free space
raise the wrong limit (nofile when it was memory)
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: under capacity pressure both disk and memory limits bite; you must triage which to relieve first.
reference_solution: Resolve 'disk_full' first: df to find the full mount; du/ncdu to find the consumer
Then resolve 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf
Validate after each step: resolvectl status
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio systemd-resolved non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (disk_full e resource_limit). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
